title: Two specified scalar comparisons for pullback along a scheme isomorphism agree
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and chosen uniformizers [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ and $W\in\{X,Y\}$ let $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$ be the derived-complete integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], let $Lg_F^*$ be the completed integral pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], and let $T_W:D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_L)$ be integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

For $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ consider two isomorphisms $T_X(Lg_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_L^*(T_YK)$:

(i) the pullback scalar comparison $a_{g,K}=\mu_{g,K}^{-1}\circ\lambda_{g,K}$ specified by the whole-system realization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], for the scheme map $f=g$ (built from the derived-limit counit of the entire quotient tower, levelwise derived change of rings and the identification $(g^*P_{E,n})\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{L,n}\cong g^*P_{L,n}$);

(ii) the tensor-and-completion comparison $\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\circ[\delta_P]\circ\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}$ specified in [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha], with $\delta_P$ the cone map induced on both cone coordinates by the level maps $d_m$ and $\chi$ the quotient-augmentation completion comparisons with zero shifted coordinate.

Then $a_{g,K}=\alpha_K$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_L)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], for every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. This is an equality of the two specified morphisms, not merely the existence of an isomorphism between their common source and target.

proof.text: Choose the simultaneous normalized realization models of [lem-trf-effective-comparison-realization-models] for $f=g$ and $E\subset L$ (take $M=L$ if a third coefficient field is required). Put $C=\mathcal R_{E,Y}K$, $A=S_XU_{g,E}C$ and $B=U_{g,L}S_YC$. Here $U,S$ and the system scalar/pullback comparison $\kappa:A\to B$ are those of [def-trf-integral-comparison-sequence-systems]. Choose the representative $P$ and $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]. The normalized models use exactly their simultaneous quotients and actual quotient transitions. All intermediate realizations are constructible and complete, and their counits are isomorphisms by the effective-model lemma. Denote the resulting source and target word-realization isomorphisms by $\beta_A:T_XLg_E^*K\to\mathcal L_LA$ and $\beta_B:Lg_L^*T_YK\to\mathcal L_LB$.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution] to the two words $S_XU_{g,E}$ and $U_{g,L}S_Y$ and their whole-system comparison $\kappa$. Its conjugation formula, using the counit at every intermediate realization, gives the counit-built completed arrow $\beta_B^{-1}\mathcal L_L(\kappa)\beta_A$. In [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] these are precisely the whole-system counits used to construct $\lambda_{g,K}$ and $\mu_{g,K}$. The former includes the balanced identification $S_XU_{g,E}C\cong U_{g,L}S_YC$; the latter realizes the target word. Consequently its specified $a_{g,K}=\mu_{g,K}^{-1}\lambda_{g,K}$ satisfies
$$\beta_B a_{g,K}=\mathcal L_L(\kappa)\beta_A.$$
This is the word-substitution theorem on entire derived systems, not a comparison of separately evaluated arrows.

proof.text:
Apply the pullback part of [lem-pur-normalized-scalar-comparison-realization] to $g,K$. Its primitive realizations have the same normalization of [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models] as in Step 1: actual quotient maps, balanced association, and the K-injective-normalized counit. Hence its normalized source and target word coordinates are $\beta_A,\beta_B$. Its finite comparison $\kappa^D$ is our $\kappa$: both are the localization of balanced scalar association on these same K-flat quotient systems. Explicitly, in the notation of [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha], scalar association followed by the quotient actions sends
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\ \longmapsto\ (g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s).$$
This is exactly $d_m$. The cited alpha statement specifies that its $\delta_P$ applies this tower map to BOTH Roos coordinates and that its $\chi$ is the quotient augmentation with zero shifted coordinate; its final paragraph identifies $\alpha_K$ with the canonical tensor-association and strict-completion comparison. This is the canonically normalized $a_F$ to which the normalized-scalar lemma applies, not a choice made from an existence isomorphism. That lemma's concluding realization assertion therefore gives
$$\beta_B\alpha_K=\mathcal L_L(\kappa)\beta_A.$$
It applies with no flatness assumption on the maps of finite quotient rings and no finite Tor-amplitude hypothesis.
